reviewer_notes: This is a meta-analysis of the ENERGY STAR ES-EPI program covering 24 industry case studies. It has been extracted as a single multi-site application (multiple registered sectors: cement, pulp & paper, iron & steel, glass, plus non-registered sectors such as dairy, food, auto assembly, pharmaceuticals, printing) with three models representing the distinct functional forms/estimation approaches the paper describes (M1 log-linear OLS, M2 stochastic frontier, M3 linear intensity form). Tables 1, 2 and 4 give per-sector instantiations: the C3 normalization variables actually included, model type, benchmark year, plant counts (14 to 775), returns-to-scale elasticities, and the 75th-to-50th percentile ranges (from -4.5 % to -43.7 %), which differ by sector and are not reproduced model-by-model here. Energy-result metrics attach only to the three sectors that received documented benchmark updates (cement -> M1; corn refining and auto assembly -> M2). No refinery or petrochemical case is present; 'corn refining' is agricultural wet milling, not petroleum refining.
